title: Nonlocal Orbital-Angular-Momentum Dichroism of Vortex Light in Strained Crystals
abstract: Vortex light carries orbital angular momentum (OAM) in its transverse phase, unlike spin, which is encoded in polarization. We show that this phase cannot produce OAM dichroism in any continuously translation-invariant system, even when optical nonlocality and multipole light--matter coupling are included. Nonuniform strain in a two-dimensional Dirac material bypasses this no-go condition by supplying transverse momentum transfer through a long-wavelength pseudo-gauge field, so that the OAM dichroism factorizes into a nonlocal elasto-optic tensor and the overlap of the vortex transverse phase current with the strain field. For a micron-scale Gaussian bubble, the resonant OAM-odd conductivity reaches \(\sim10^{-3}e^2/\hbar\), within reach of differential optical measurements.
summary: This paper theoretically demonstrates that OAM dichroism in vortex light is forbidden in uniform crystalline media. By introducing nonuniform strain into a 2D Dirac material, the authors show how transverse momentum transfer can be supplied via a pseudo-gauge field. This allows for a measurable, non-zero OAM-odd optical conductivity, opening a pathway for differential optical measurements of strain effects.
main_problem: The research investigates the mechanism by which Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) dichroism of vortex light can be generated in condensed matter systems, overcoming theoretical no-go theorems.
main_result: Nonuniform strain in a 2D Dirac material bypasses the no-go condition, allowing for a measurable OAM-odd conductivity ($\sim 10^{-3}e^2/\hbar$) through the coupling of vortex phase current with the strain field.
method: The analysis uses theoretical derivations involving nonlocal response functions, factorizing the dichroism into an elasto-optic tensor and a geometric overlap term derived from Green's function techniques.
model_or_system: The model employs a two-dimensional Dirac material Hamiltonian, specifically incorporating nonuniform strain (modeled as a Gaussian bubble) to break translational symmetry. The analysis considers both interband and intraband contributions to the optical response.
key_observables: OAM dichroism ($\Delta\sigma_{OAM}$), nonlocal elasto-optic tensor ($\Lambda^{(s)}_{ab}$), and Geometric Overlap Tensor ($B^{(\ell)}_{ab}$).
important_parameters: Strain amplitude ($\alpha$), beam waist ($w_0$), bubble displacement ($d$), and the ratio of material parameters defining valley inequivalence.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative expansions in strain/momentum transfer (Q) and assumes specific limits for integrals, such as $k=0$ for intraband calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup (vortex light on strained material), show the dependence of the geometric overlap term on displacement, and plot resonant enhancements of material coefficients near resonance.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the no-go theorem for OAM dichroism in translationally invariant systems. It then introduces strain as the necessary symmetry breaker, developing theoretical frameworks to calculate the nonlocal elasto-optic tensor ($\Lambda$) and the geometric overlap ($B$). Finally, it calculates these terms for specific Dirac models.
why_interesting: This work connects topological light properties (OAM) with material strain engineering in 2D electron systems, providing a concrete mechanism for optical detection of subtle symmetry breaking effects relevant to condensed matter physics.

The sur- face represents a Gaussian strain bubble, with colour indicat- ing the deformation amplitude. The vortex core is displaced from the bubble center by the in-plane vector d. The circular arrows denote the vortex transverse phase current J (ℓ). This relative displacement breaks the common circular symmetry of the optical and strain profiles, enabling OAM-sensitive cou- pling through optical nonlocality.
